title: Project Files — folders open at any size

steps.headline: Every folder opens straight from your disk, at any size and any depth — no "Browse anyway" screen.
steps.changed: The Files tab now reads just the folder you open, a page at a time, instead of scanning the whole project first. Folder cards count what is directly inside ("1 item") rather than everything beneath ("1 file").
steps.measured: A 2,000-file folder draws 1,230 page elements, down from 11,124
steps.notice: Your home folder and whole drives open like any other project. Folders more than 6 levels deep, hidden folders like .git, node_modules and projects inside projects now appear and open. Huge folders load more as you scroll.
steps.risk: Code projects now show folders they used to hide (.git, node_modules), so the top level looks busier. Search still stops at 2,000 files with its note until the next stage.

steps.path: Projects → Files, a folder your computer won't let the app read
steps.headline: A folder your computer blocks now says so, with Retry, instead of looking empty.
steps.changed: When the system refuses to open a folder, or a drive is unplugged, the Files tab shows the real reason and a Retry button. Before, such a folder simply showed nothing.
steps.notice: The breadcrumb stays above it, so one click on Project Files takes you back out.
